item.title: Version 1.0.5
item.description:
What's New in 1.0.5

New

  • TrixCode now automatically restarts its AI server whenever you add or remove MCP servers — no manual restart needed to pick up your changes.

Improved

  • Updated the Xcode Build integration to version 4, bringing the latest build tools and capabilities to your workflow.
  • The Figma MCP preset now correctly connects to the local Desktop plugin endpoint, making it easier to pull designs straight into your coding session.

Fixed

  • The message input box now scrolls properly when you type a long prompt — no more text disappearing off the bottom.

item.title: Version 1.0.4
item.description:
What's New in 1.0.4

New

  • You can now add and remove MCP servers directly within TrixCode, with full OAuth support for servers that require authentication.

Improved

  • Error messages are now clearer and more descriptive, so you spend less time guessing what went wrong.

Fixed

  • Permission prompts and questions from AI sub-agents are now handled in order, preventing chats from getting stuck waiting for a response.

item.title: Version 1.0.3
item.description:
What's New in 1.0.3

New

  • Added an About window with a link to support TrixCode on Ko-fi — tips are always appreciated and help keep the project going!
  • You can now paste images from your clipboard or drag and drop them directly into the chat input, making it easier to share screenshots of errors, UI issues, or code snippets.

Improved

  • TrixCode now remembers which AI model you had selected for each session. Switching providers also automatically validates your model choice, so you'll never accidentally be talking to the wrong model.

item.title: Version 1.0.2
item.description:
What's New in 1.0.2

New

  • @mention file search: Type @ in the message input to quickly search and reference files from your project — no more copy-pasting paths.
  • Context window breakdown: A new popover shows you exactly how your context window is being used, with a clear token-by-token breakdown so you always know what's being sent to the model.
  • File diffs after responses: When the assistant modifies files, a diff is displayed inline after its response so you can review changes at a glance.
  • Slash command palette: Type / to bring up a command palette with MCP tools and quick actions — a faster way to drive the assistant without leaving the chat.
  • Global hotkey support: Set a system-wide keyboard shortcut to bring TrixCode into focus from anywhere, even when Xcode is front and centre. Configure it in the new Hotkeys settings tab.
  • OAuth device authorization: Providers that support OAuth can now be authenticated with a simple device flow — just follow the link, approve access, and you're connected.
  • Todo panel: The assistant can now maintain a live todo list during longer coding sessions, keeping track of outstanding tasks as it works through your requests.
  • Auto-updates via Sparkle: TrixCode can now update itself. Use Check for Updates in the menu bar to grab the latest version without visiting GitHub.
  • Rebuilt onboarding: A refreshed, eight-step onboarding flow walks you through setup more clearly, including accessibility permissions and provider configuration.

Improved

  • XcodeBuildMCP is now zero-setup: The XcodeBuildMCP tool ships as a self-contained binary inside TrixCode — nothing to install or configure separately.
  • Streaming text is back to normal: A bug was preventing streamed responses from rendering word-by-word as the model replied. This is now fixed and responses flow in smoothly again.
  • Providers load without an open project: You no longer need an active project directory open before your AI providers become available.
  • Selected code context: Highlighted code in Xcode is picked up automatically and attached as context when you send a message — no manual copy-paste required.
  • Model, agent, and variant selectors: Easily switch between models and agent configurations directly from the chat interface.
  • Structured server logs: Server output is now captured in a structured log store, making it much easier to diagnose connection issues when something goes wrong.
  • Window management improvements: TrixCode now enforces a sensible minimum window height and handles multi-display layouts more reliably. The onboarding card no longer overflows on smaller screens.
  • Xcode window tracking fixed: TrixCode was occasionally latching onto dialogs and popups instead of the Xcode editor window. It now correctly follows your editor.
  • Faster reconnection on project switch: Switching between Xcode projects reconnects to the backend more reliably and quickly.
  • Settings screen: A dedicated Settings panel brings together provider authentication, model selection, OAuth flows, and hotkey configuration in one place.

Fixed

  • Fixed a crash that could occur during server startup when first registering an MCP tool.
  • Fixed an issue where the app window would not restore correctly across displays.
  • Fixed a race condition with project pinning that could leave the app in an inconsistent state on launch.
  • Fixed SSE connection drops not recovering properly when switching projects.
  • Fixed provider type decoding errors that could silently prevent models from loading.
